questions.stem:
Case study: Bisi, Kunle and Musa run a successful catering partnership in Ibadan. Demand has grown, and they now want to open branches in Lagos and Abuja, buy delivery vans and a large cold room. Their bank has refused further loans because the partners have unlimited liability and little security. A consultant advises them to convert the business into a private limited company. Kunle fears that he will lose control, while Musa worries about the legal formalities and costs.
(a) Explain two disadvantages of the partnership form of business that the case reveals. [6 marks]
(b) Explain three advantages the partners would gain by converting to a private limited company. [9 marks]
(c) State four documents or steps required to register a private limited company in Nigeria. [6 marks]
(d) Advise the partners on two other sources of finance for the expansion. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: unlimited liability: partners' personal assets are at risk, discouraging lenders
3 marks: limited capital/borrowing capacity restricts expansion
3 marks: limited liability protects personal assets of members
3 marks: easier to raise capital by issuing shares and obtaining loans
3 marks: separate legal entity and perpetual succession / continuity
2 marks: reservation of company name with the Corporate Affairs Commission
2 marks: preparation of memorandum and articles of association
2 marks: filing statement of share capital, particulars of directors and payment of fees to obtain certificate of incorporation
2 marks: venture capital / admitting new shareholders (equity)
2 marks: hire purchase or leasing of vans and equipment / government SME loans (e.g. BOI)
questions.explanation: The partnership's unlimited liability and limited borrowing power block expansion. A private company offers limited liability, easier capital raising, separate legal personality and continuity; control can be preserved by share allocation. Registration with the CAC involves name reservation, memorandum and articles, statement of share capital and directors' particulars, fees and the certificate of incorporation. Other finance: new equity investors, venture capital, leasing or hire purchase, and government SME loan schemes.

questions.stem:
(a) Define motivation. [3 marks]
(b) Explain the five levels of Maslow's hierarchy of needs. [10 marks]
(c) State one limitation of Maslow's theory. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: the inner drive or process that stimulates a person to act towards achieving a goal
2 marks: physiological needs: food, water, shelter
2 marks: safety needs: security, job security, protection
2 marks: social needs: love, friendship, belonging
2 marks: esteem needs: recognition, status, respect
2 marks: self-actualisation: realising one's full potential
2 marks: needs may not follow a fixed order / individuals and cultures differ
questions.explanation: Motivation is the drive that causes people to act towards goals. Maslow ranked needs as physiological, safety, social, esteem and self-actualisation, each becoming important when lower needs are satisfied. Critics note that people do not always follow this order and cultural differences matter.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain four elements of a valid contract. [8 marks]
(b) Explain three ways by which a contract may be discharged. [6 marks]
(c) What is a void contract? [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: offer: a definite proposal by one party
2 marks: acceptance: unconditional agreement to the offer
2 marks: consideration: something of value given by each party
2 marks: capacity / intention to create legal relations / legality of object
2 marks: performance: both parties fulfil their obligations
2 marks: agreement: parties mutually agree to end the contract
2 marks: breach / frustration / operation of law
1 mark: a contract that has no legal effect from the beginning
questions.explanation: Elements include offer, acceptance, consideration, capacity, intention and legality. Contracts are discharged by performance, agreement, breach, frustration or operation of law. A void contract has no legal effect at all.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five functions of the Central Bank of Nigeria. [10 marks]
(b) Distinguish between a current account and a savings account. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: issues the national currency
2 marks: banker to the government
2 marks: banker to commercial banks / lender of last resort
2 marks: regulates and supervises banks
2 marks: implements monetary policy / manages external reserves
2 marks: current account: cheques can be used for withdrawals
1 mark: current account usually earns no interest and may allow overdraft
2 marks: savings account: earns interest and is used mainly to save, with withdrawals restricted
questions.explanation: The CBN issues currency, banks for government and banks, acts as lender of last resort, regulates banks, conducts monetary policy and manages reserves. A current account uses cheques, earns little or no interest and may allow overdrafts; a savings account earns interest and is for saving.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the term human resource management. [3 marks]
(b) Describe four steps in the recruitment and selection process. [8 marks]
(c) State two types of training given to employees. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: the management of people in an organisation, covering recruitment, training, compensation, welfare and employee relations
2 marks: identifying the vacancy and preparing a job description/specification
2 marks: advertising the vacancy
2 marks: shortlisting and testing/interviewing applicants
2 marks: selecting, offering appointment and induction
2 marks: on-the-job training
2 marks: off-the-job training / induction / apprenticeship
questions.explanation: HRM manages people: recruitment, training, pay, welfare and relations. Steps: job analysis, advertisement, screening and interviews, selection, appointment and induction. Training may be on-the-job, off-the-job, induction or apprenticeship.

questions.stem:
(a) Define entrepreneurship. [3 marks]
(b) List six items contained in a business plan. [6 marks]
(c) Explain three reasons why small businesses fail. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: the process of identifying opportunities and organising resources to create a business, bearing the risk for profit
1 mark: executive summary
1 mark: description of the business and products
1 mark: market analysis
1 mark: marketing strategy
1 mark: management and organisation
1 mark: financial plan / funding requirements
2 marks: poor management and record keeping
2 marks: inadequate capital
2 marks: poor location / stiff competition / lack of planning / poor infrastructure
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurship is identifying opportunities and combining resources to start a business while bearing risk. A business plan covers summary, business description, market analysis, marketing, management, operations and finance. Small businesses fail through poor management, inadequate capital, bad location, competition and poor planning.
